summary: Administrative groups are link attributes used for traffic engineering. This document defines a BGP-LS extension to advertise extended administrative groups (EAGs).

eli5.summary: Links can be given colored tags to guide traffic choices. This document lets longer tag sets be shared through BGP-LS.

questions: what is an extended administrative group
what are link colors in traffic engineering
how long is the eag tlv
subtitle: A new BGP-LS TLV that carries extended administrative groups, the longer link colors used in traffic engineering.

tldr.problem: Administrative groups ('link colors') were a fixed 32-bit bitmask that proved too small, and extended administrative groups (EAGs) had no way to be passed on to BGP-LS consumers.
tldr.mechanism: The document defines a new BGP-LS Link Attribute TLV, type 1173, holding one or more 32-bit bitmasks.
tldr.outcome: A BGP-LS speaker can now tell a centralized controller the EAGs of links, so the controller can use them in traffic engineering computations.

today: RFC 9104 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2021. It has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Administrative groups, commonly called colors or link colors, are link attributes advertised by link-state protocols such as IS-IS, OSPFv2 and OSPFv3. In BGP-LS (Border Gateway Protocol - Link State), the original non-extended administrative groups are encoded using the Administrative Group (color) TLV 1088 defined in RFC 7752.

This document specifies an extension to BGP-LS for advertising the extended administrative groups.
sections.eli5: Network links can carry colored tags. BGP-LS is a way of reporting the network's map to a planning program, and this note teaches it to report one more kind of tag.

sections.title: Why Extended Groups Exist
sections.content:
The original administrative groups are a fixed-length 32-bit bitmask. As networks grew and more use cases appeared, 32 bits became constraining, so extended administrative groups (EAGs) were introduced in RFC 7308.

The new EAG TLV does not replace the Administrative Group (color) TLV. As RFC 7308 explains, both values can coexist. How a BGP-LS consumer behaves is out of scope for this document.
sections.eli5: The old tag list only had room for 32 colors. When that ran out, a longer list was created, and the old list stays around alongside it.

sections.title: The EAG TLV
sections.content:
BGP-LS speakers use the new TLV to signal the EAG of links to a consumer of topology data, such as a centralized controller, which can use the information in traffic engineering computations and other use cases. When the speaker originates topology learned from OSPF or IS-IS, the EAG information is taken from the underlying extensions in RFC 7308.

The TLV is a new Link Attribute TLV with Type 1173. The Length is the total length of the value field in octets and MUST be a multiple of 4; if it is not, the TLV MUST be considered malformed. The value is one or more 32-bit bitmasks, and a set bit means the corresponding administrative group (color) is enabled on the link.
sections.eli5: The tag list is sent as a labeled package: a label saying what it is, a size, and then the colors in chunks of the same size. If the size is not a whole number of chunks, the package is thrown out as broken.

sections.title: IANA Code Point
sections.content: IANA has assigned code point 1173 from the 'BGP-LS Node Descriptor, Link Descriptor, Prefix Descriptor, and Attribute TLVs' registry. Its description is Extended Administrative Group, and it corresponds to IS-IS TLV/Sub-TLV 22/14.
sections.eli5: The number 1173 is now officially reserved for this kind of tag list, so nobody else uses it.

sections.title: Manageability
sections.content:
The extension adds to the existing IGP topology information distributed through RFC 7752 and does not affect BGP protocol operations and management, other than as discussed in Section 6 of RFC 7752. The syntactic checks for malformed attributes now cover the new TLV.

Semantic or content checking of the TLV, and its association with BGP-LS NLRI types or attributes, is left to the consumer of the information (an application or controller) and not to BGP itself.
sections.eli5: BGP only checks that the package is built correctly. Deciding what the colors mean is up to the planning program that reads them.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extension does not affect the BGP security model. The document only introduces a new Attribute TLV, and any syntactic error in it would result in the BGP-LS Attribute being discarded. The TLV propagates the EAG extensions from RFC 7308, and the IGP instances originating it are assumed to support any required OSPF and IS-IS security mechanisms.

The advertisement of this link attribute information presents no significant additional risk beyond the link attribute information already supported in RFC 7752.
sections.eli5: Sharing these extra tags is no riskier than sharing the other link information already shared, and a broken package is just ignored.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: Code point assigned for the TLV.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Length of the value field in octets; MUST be a multiple of 4.

fields.name: Extended Administrative Group
fields.desc: One or more 32-bit bitmasks; the field is variable length.
